title: Developmental Persistence, Executive Function, and Intellectual Compensation in ADHD
background: This module evaluates persistence of ADHD-related executive and functional impairment and whether intelligence or achievement may compensate for, mask, or delay recognition of impairment.
population: Adolescents and adults with diagnosed ADHD or validated ADHD traits, including high-intelligence or high-achievement subgroups.
intervention: Developmental persistence, executive dysfunction, intelligence, achievement, compensation, masking, or delayed recognition.
comparator: Controls without ADHD, lower-intelligence or lower-achievement groups, remitted ADHD, or within-person developmental follow-up.

outcomes_primary.name: Persistence of symptoms or executive/functional impairment
Evidence for or against intelligence-related compensation or delayed recognition

outcomes_secondary.name: Cross-setting impairment, effort, instability, quality of life, and alternative explanations

inclusion: Adolescent or adult ADHD population, or developmental follow-up into adulthood.
Evaluates persistence, executive/functional outcomes, intelligence, achievement, compensation, masking, or recognition.
Uses a defined diagnostic or validated trait measure.
Reports empirical results or an authoritative evidence synthesis.
exclusion: Pediatric-only report without developmental relevance beyond adolescence.
No separable ADHD population or validated ADHD-trait analysis.
Opinion, advocacy, protocol, or unsourced narrative without systematic empirical data.
No outcome relevant to claims H1 or H2.
registration: Protocol frozen for AI-assisted rapid review on 2026-07-29; not prospectively registered.
disclaimer: AI Reviewer-1 rapid-review draft. Human Reviewer 2 and clinical sign-off remain pending. Not diagnostic or treatment guidance.
